doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Dedications and Inspirations
summary: Solo album with tunes for painters and Hawkins.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: No, no, (overlapping/inaudible). It’s interesting that as we’re talking about some of these albums, you know, that certain things sort of stand out.
About people who are, who have been important to you…
…or influenced you or inspired you. And I’m thinking of two completely different albums now that relate to that in my mind.
One is the Dedications and Inspirations, which was a solo album.
I’m not sure. Probably. I’m not even sure, Deb. Yeah, that was…
Do you remember what’s on there? Because I can… there’s some interesting things that relate to…
Oh, yeah. I tried to get certain painters in my mind, I guess, and then improvise something that, that would maybe suggest that.
Yep. You have a tune called Miró.
And those are both on that album. There’s a tune dedicated to Coleman Hawkins.

Oh, that’s wild. Yeah. Yeah, I’d have to hear that again. But obviously, I really admired him. And I guess I just tried to… I think they were all improvised, basically. So I just tried to aurally visualize Coleman Hawkins playing and make some sound like that, I guess. And I think I did one for Charlie Christian, as well. I can’t remember but…
